title: Days-Supply Rule Sheet: Specialty Transition Supply (Formulary Benefit)
content:
**Rule.** A specialty transition supply under the Formulary Benefit covers as many dose cycles as the member's latest shipped specialty fill of the drug contained. One dose cycle is the days supply of that latest shipped fill divided by its quantity. The days supply of the specialty transition supply is the number of dose cycles multiplied by the length of one dose cycle. The result is never less than zero and never more than the formulary's maximum days supply for one transition fill, and it is taken as a whole number of days.

## Inputs and where they are read

| Input | Record |
|---|---|
| days supply of the latest shipped fill | the member's shipped specialty fills of the drug, latest by ship date |
| quantity of the latest shipped fill | same fill |
| formulary's maximum days supply for one transition fill | the member's Northbridge formulary |

## Calculation in order

1. The length of one dose cycle is the fill's days supply divided by its quantity.
2. The number of dose cycles is the fill's quantity.
3. The supply is the number of dose cycles multiplied by the cycle length.
4. The supply is held to no less than zero and no more than the formulary's maximum for one transition fill, and is taken in whole days.

## Worked figures (hypothetical fills, on a formulary whose maximum for one transition fill is 30 days)

| Latest shipped fill | Cycle length | Dose cycles | Product | Specialty transition supply |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 days, quantity 2 | 14 days | 2 | 28 days | 28 days |
| 84 days, quantity 6 | 14 days | 6 | 84 days | 30 days (held at the maximum) |
| 30 days, quantity 4 | 7.5 days | 4 | 30 days | 30 days |
